product_name: Jaggery Blocks

review_notes: Jaggery is a traditional South Asian unrefined whole cane/palm sugar -- nutritionally it is essentially concentrated sucrose with trace minerals, the same risk category as brown sugar despite the unfamiliar (to a US rule engine's typical lexicon) regional name. GroceryDB was searched directly for 'jaggery' across its full catalog; the only three hits were an unrelated samosa, a vegan chicken wrap, and a paneer product where 'jaggery' did not actually appear as a sugar ingredient (false keyword matches on 'paneer'), so no real, correctly-labeled jaggery product exists in the dataset to draw from -- hand-composed as a single-ingredient product to isolate the term cleanly.

product_name: Panela Cane Sugar Cones
ingredients_raw: Panela (Unrefined Whole Cane Sugar).
review_notes: Panela (also called piloncillo) is the Latin American equivalent of jaggery -- unrefined whole cane sugar sold in solid cones or blocks, functionally identical to brown/raw sugar. GroceryDB's real 'panela' hits were all Panela CHEESE (a Mexican fresh cheese that happens to share the name with the sugar) -- confirmed by reading their ingredient lists, which were pasteurized milk/salt/enzyme with no sugar at all -- so using any of those would have mislabeled a dairy product as a sugar example. Hand-composed instead to correctly represent the actual sugar product this name refers to.

product_name: Gur (Unrefined Sugarcane Jaggery)
ingredients_raw: Gur (Sugarcane Juice, Concentrated and Solidified).
review_notes: 'Gur' is the Hindi/Punjabi name for the same unrefined cane sugar product called jaggery elsewhere in South Asia -- included as a separate record because a rule engine's lexicon might catch one regional name and not its synonym. A GroceryDB search for 'gur' returned only false-positive substring matches (e.g. 'yogurt', 'gurus' in a bakery name, ingredient words containing the letters 'gur') with no actual gur/jaggery product, confirming this concept genuinely has no clean real-product example available in the dataset -- hand-composed to isolate the term.

product_name: Date Syrup Sweetener Bottle
ingredients_raw: Date Syrup (100% Dates).
review_notes: Included as a clean, single-ingredient positive control for 'date syrup used as a standalone sweetener product' (as opposed to the several GroceryDB-sourced records in this set where date syrup/paste is one ingredient among many in a sauce or bar). GroceryDB does contain 'date syrup' as an ingredient inside composite products (several sauces in this set use it), but no standalone date-syrup bottle product, so this isolates the case: date syrup is fruit-derived (natural_sugar_context true) but functions entirely as a concentrated added sweetener when sold and used this way, at a very high sugar density (roughly 65g/100g is typical for date syrup, comparable to honey) -- hence HIGH despite the 'natural' framing.
